The normal components of LPG are propane (C H ) and butane (C H ). Small 3 8 4 10 concentrations of other hydrocarbons may also be present. LPG at atmospheric pressure and temperature becomes a gas which has a relative density to air of 1.5 to 2.0 and is readily liquefied under moderate pressures. The relative density of LPG liquid to water is approximately 0.53 to 0.58 at 15°C. LPG has a flash point at atmospheric pressure of -42°C and becomes a flammable mixture in air at a concentration of 1.5% (LFL) to 9.6% (UFL). The LPG Terminal primary storage area is approximately 1,000 feet away from the eastern extent of the proposed T-RICH plant layout and is surrounded by extensive berms and fire water monitors. Refer to Fig. 3.14. It is not expected that the terminal property and the associated LPG storage dome will present a significant enough risk to the T-RICH site that it would require additional risk mitigation. Additionally, the LPG marine transfer pipeline to the north is not considered to be a significant threat to the T-RICH site due to its location, infrequent usage (reported to be less than 3 times per year), and the potential to generate a large persistent fire of sufficient magnitude to pose a significant hazard to T-RICH equipment and personnel. However, it is recommended that in FEED the project review any existing Facility Siting or Major Process Hazard Analysis documentation that should exist for the Plains LPG terminal property and operations in order to verify the above assumptions. The highest risk associated with LPG handling is considered to be fires or explosions related to the LPG railcar marshalling and loading facilities along the southern portion of the T-RICH Site (see Fig. 3.14). Entr has performed a coarse review potential fire and explosion magnitudes and frequencies of occurrence based on experience and generic industry data. The conclusion was that explosions from a railcar rupture or BLEVE or a large railcar operations related leak generating an LPG vapor cloud explosion (VCE) requires further evaluation in FEED if explosion risk analyses for Plains LPG assets are unavailable (i.e. a Facility Siting Study).
